```{r}
#-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+
library(spatstat)
library(RColorBrewer)
data(longleaf)
```

```{r}
#-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+
# function to automate K to L conversion 
KtoL <- function(Kobj){
    # Function to convert Kest objects to Lest objects
    list(
        r=Kobj$r,
        obs=sqrt(Kobj$obs / pi) - Kobj$r,
        lo=sqrt(Kobj$lo / pi) - Kobj$r,
        hi=sqrt(Kobj$hi / pi) - Kobj$r,
        theo=sqrt(Kobj$theo / pi) - Kobj$r
    )
}
```


```{r}
#-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+
# notice here how we pass additional, unspecified arguments to the plot function!
# we use that in the final lines of this demo to provide a title using the "main"
# argument to plot
# plotting function - use this for HW 
PlotKenvAsL <- function(Kobj, poly_col="#BDD7E7", obs_col="#636363", exp_col="#A50F15", ...){
    # Function to make nice plots of Kest envelope objects transformed to L
    Lobj <- KtoL(Kobj)
    polyx <- c(Lobj$r, rev(Lobj$r))
    polyy <- c(Lobj$lo, rev(Lobj$hi))
    xlim <- range(Lobj$r)
    ylim <- range(c(Lobj$obs, Lobj$theo, Lobj$lo, Lobj$hi))
    plot(NA, NA, xlim=xlim, ylim=ylim, type="n", xlab=expression(italic("r")), ylab=expression(italic("L(r)")), ...)
    polygon(x=polyx, y=polyy, col=poly_col, border=NA)
    points(Lobj$r, Lobj$obs, type="l", lty=1, col=obs_col, lwd=2)
    if(length(Lobj$theo) > 0) points(Lobj$r, Lobj$theo, type="l", lty=2, col=exp_col)
}
```

#-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+
# Quick notes on rshift.ppp(x)
# There is a difference between marked and "multitype" ppp
# If x is multitype, then each grouping/type is shifted separately
# If it's not multitype, then you need to provide the "group" parameters
# To get toroidal shift, you need to specify "edge=torus"
# Toroidal shifts only make sense for rectangular windows

#-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+
```{r}
# rshift example
t_red <- rgb(t(col2rgb(brewer.pal(5, "Reds")[4])), max=255, alpha=0.5*255)
t_blue <- rgb(t(col2rgb(brewer.pal(5, "Blues")[4])), max=255, alpha=0.5*255)
plot_cols <- c(t_red, t_blue) # transparent red/blue for bivariate ppp
```


```{r}
# change the marks to "J" and "A" for juvenile and adults
tmp <- longleaf
marks(tmp) <- rep("J", length(marks(longleaf)))
marks(tmp)[marks(longleaf) >= 25] <- "A"
```


```{r}
# compare rshift options
# the rshift function is very important to understand 
layout(matrix(1:4, nrow=2, byrow=T))
plot(tmp, cols=plot_cols, chars=16, cex=1.5, main="longleaf") # original pattern
# rshift w/o specifying "group" shifts everything together
# this is the torodial shift with no groups 
# only supply the edge arguments - the patterns are exactly the same but both the patterns are shifted 
plot(rshift(tmp, edge="torus"), cols=plot_cols, chars=16, cex=1.5, main="toroidal, no groups")
# rshift specifying group (as a factor!) shifts each one independently
plot(rshift(tmp, group=as.factor(marks(tmp)), edge="torus"), cols=plot_cols, chars=16, cex=1.5, main="toroidal, both groups shifted ind.")
# rshift with groups, and using "which" to shift just juvenile ("J") types
# the which argument measn that you only shift one group 
# for the purpose of the null, it does not matter which ppp you are shifting 
plot(rshift(tmp, group=as.factor(marks(tmp)), which="J", edge="torus"), cols=plot_cols, chars=16, cex=1.5, main="toroidal, one group shifted")
```


#-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+
```{r}
# rlabel example
layout(matrix(1:3, nrow=1))
plot(tmp, cols=plot_cols, chars=16, cex=1.5, main="longleaf") # original pattern
plot(rlabel(tmp), cols=plot_cols, chars=16, cex=1.5, main="label perm 1") # random label perm
plot(rlabel(tmp), cols=plot_cols, chars=16, cex=1.5, main="label perm 2") # random lable perm
# notice that the original pattern is preserved, just the "J" or "A" designation is changed
```

```{r}
#-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+
# univariate point patterns
# can use the envelope command to create the envelope for 
ll_env_juv <- envelope(longleaf[marks(longleaf) <=15 ], Kest)
ll_env_mat <- envelope(longleaf[marks(longleaf) >= 25 ], Kest)
layout(matrix(1:2, nrow=1))
PlotKenvAsL(ll_env_juv)
PlotKenvAsL(ll_env_mat)
```
```{r}
# Important: the default method of simulating reference point patterns w/ envelope is CSR!
# bivariate w/ envelopes from default method (CSR but the right number of relative marks)
# far fewer J group around A group than we expect
# But this is wrong because it does not perserve the spatial pattterns of the input data - i.e. it does not do the torodial shift 
ll_env_csr <- envelope(longleaf, Kmulti, I=marks(longleaf) <= 15, J=marks(longleaf) >= 25)
PlotKenvAsL(ll_env_csr)
```


```{r}
# to test independence of point pattern processes, conditioned on univariate patterns, we
# need a toroidal shift (which we can do since this is a rectangular window) that shifts one
# or both of the juvenile and adult patterns independently, but preserves each univariate pattern
# we can use rshift, but keep in mind that we must use "group" since this isn't a multitype ppp
# we'll also define a function to supply the marks and use that for "I" and "J"
# Need to simulate the expression BEFORE you evaluate the marks - so that marks aren't set in stone and be assigned correctly 
fJ <- function(x) marks(x) <= 15
fA <- function(x) marks(x) >= 25
# This is the correct way to do inference 
# there is still a range between 4 and 25 where there are fewer A points near B points - can be confident that replusion is happening at these scales 
ll_env_toroidal <- envelope(longleaf, Kmulti, I=fJ, J=fA, simulate=expression(rshift(longleaf, group=as.factor(marks(longleaf)<=15), edge="torus")))
PlotKenvAsL(ll_env_toroidal)
```

```{r}
# we can verify that rshift() is doing what we expect, and demonstrate that we could supply
# any sort of custom function to the "simulate" argument of envelope()
# Josh is writing his own shift function
MyShift <- function(x){
    # performs toroidal shift on the longleaf dataset
    # by shifting each juvenile and adult univariate ppp independently
    x_a <- longleaf[marks(longleaf) <= 15]
    x_b <- longleaf[marks(longleaf) >= 25]
    x_a <- rshift(x_a, edge="torus")
    x_b <- rshift(x_b, edge="torus")
    X <- superimpose(x_a, x_b)
    return(X)
}
```


```{r}
ll_env_toroidal_byhand <- envelope(longleaf, Kmulti, I=fJ, J=fA, simulate=expression(MyShift(longleaf)))
```

```{r}
# plot them together to see that they're close enough to be convinced that differences are
# probably due to stochastic simulation processes and a relatively small set of simulations
# you can use the "nsim" argument to envelope() to increase the number of simulations, and thus
# gain greater certainty about the envelopes, but pay attention to "nrank" argument and read the
# full envelope() help so you'll know which values are plotted
# There is an element of stochasticity in this process
layout(matrix(1:2, nrow=1))
PlotKenvAsL(ll_env_toroidal_byhand)
PlotKenvAsL(ll_env_toroidal)
```

```{r}
#-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+
# what about a label permutation? Well, that's a bit easier using rlabel()
# first, let's see what it does:
layout(matrix(1:4, nrow=2))
plot(longleaf, main="original")
plot(rlabel(longleaf), main="perm 1")
plot(rlabel(longleaf), main="perm 2")
plot(rlabel(longleaf), main="perm 3")
# note that the locations are preserved, but the marks have been randomly reassigned
```


```{r}
# first try...
ll_env_labelperm <- envelope(longleaf, Kmulti, I=marks(longleaf) <= 15, J=marks(longleaf) >= 25, simulate=expression(rlabel(longleaf)))
PlotKenvAsL(ll_env_labelperm)
```

```{r}
# why don't we have an envelope?
# We undid all the scrambling that we did first - that's why the low and high boundaries are the same and thus no confidence envlope was not created 
# need to think about the order critcially - need to use the F and J function to get around this 
names(ll_env_labelperm)
identical(ll_env_labelperm$lo, ll_env_labelperm$hi) # so the upper and lower bounds are the same?
# the thing is, our "simulate=" expression was fine, but since we specified the I and J args
# to envelope() by referencing the original longleaf dataset, and we don't change the point locations
# we just end up reassigning the labels. That is, we undo the permutation w/ our I and J expression
# we need to instead write functions, as above, that assign the labels based on the marks of each
```

```{r}
# simulated point pattern independently (borrowing the same functions as above)
# Josh would argue for the torodial shift approach in this case 
ll_env_labelperm <- envelope(longleaf, Kmulti, I=fJ, J=fA, simulate=expression(rlabel(longleaf)))
PlotKenvAsL(ll_env_labelperm)
```
```{r}
#-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+
# now let's plot them all together
layout(matrix(1:3, nrow=1))
PlotKenvAsL(ll_env_csr, main="Default envelope() CSR")
PlotKenvAsL(ll_env_toroidal, main="Toroidal Shift", poly_col=brewer.pal(5, "Reds")[2])
PlotKenvAsL(ll_env_labelperm, main="Label Permutation", poly_col=brewer.pal(5, "Greens")[2])
# default envelope - no spatial pattern preserved 
# toroidal - right approach - breaking the spatial relationship 
# label permuation - wrong bc the process did not decide whether the tree is juvenile or adult - looks more at the interaction between the points 
```
